hook: Redwood Park: half an acre of coast redwoods at the foot of the Transamerica Pyramid.

historic_status.reason: National Register Individual, Historic Resource Evaluation Response

public_open_space.name: Redwood Park
public_open_space.description: This extensively landscaped urban park offers redwood trees at the foot of the Transamerica Pyramid. It features, a tall water fountain, sculptures, and ample seating.
public_open_space.landscaping: Many redwood trees, diverse ground cover and plantings, flowers, shrubs. Multiple smaller spaces defined within park
public_open_space.seating: 100+ linear seats on boxes, room for 30+ on steps. No movable.

narrative.lead: Thomas Galli designed the park in 1969 alongside William Pereira's pyramid; it was built and planted in 1972.

sections.heading: Eighty redwoods, fifty left
sections.body: The original planting brought eighty mature coast redwoods down from the Santa Cruz Mountains. Fifty remain. A bronze by Glenna Goodacre was added in 1989 and Richard Clopton's frogs and lily pads in 1996.
